questions.q: How long does a team wait today for a new environment to run its application?
questions.why: Platform speed is the main reason teams adopt it.
questions.need: A team gets a new environment in under an hour
questions.how: Offer clusters or namespaces from templates, self-service
questions.listen: Days of waiting for an environment is the delay the business feels.
questions.probe: What do teams do while they wait: build their own, or open a cloud account?

questions.q: Who is responsible for a cluster's upgrades today, and how far behind are they?
questions.why: Upgrade debt is the most common hidden risk.
questions.need: Cluster upgrades have an owner and are current
questions.how: Name the owner and agree an upgrade cadence
questions.listen: Clusters several versions behind are unsupported and risky; upgrading them by hand is the cost.
questions.probe: How long did the last cluster upgrade take, and what broke?

questions.q: How many clusters exist, including the ones teams created themselves?
questions.need: Every cluster is known, team-made ones included
questions.how: Attach every cluster to central management
questions.listen: Clusters built by teams themselves are the sprawl to bring under one management.
questions.probe: Which distributions and clouds are they on?

questions.q: Which workloads keep data in volumes, and is that data backed up?
questions.why: Stateful workloads are the ones that lose data.
questions.need: Data in volumes is backed up and restorable
questions.how: Back up stateful workloads and test one restore
questions.listen: Stateful workloads without backups are a recovery gap; many assume the cluster protects them.
questions.probe: Has anyone restored a stateful application from backup, and how long did it take?

questions.q: What stops a team from deploying an unapproved image or a privileged pod?
questions.why: Policy at admission is where security becomes routine.
questions.need: Unapproved images and privileged pods are refused
questions.how: Turn on admission policies, first in audit mode
questions.listen: Without admission rules, one deployment can open the whole cluster.
questions.probe: Who decides which base images are approved, and how is it enforced?

questions.q: Are changes made through Git, or by hand on the cluster?
questions.why: Hand changes are the source of drift and outages.
questions.need: Changes go through Git, not by hand
questions.how: Move one team to GitOps and show the drift it removes
questions.listen: Changes made by hand drift; Git gives history and clusters that can be rebuilt.
questions.probe: Could a lost cluster be rebuilt from Git alone?

questions.q: Could each team tell you what its workloads cost last month?
questions.why: Cost visibility changes behaviour more than budgets.
questions.need: Each team sees what its workloads cost
questions.how: Turn on cost per namespace and share it monthly
questions.listen: No cost per team means no reason to clean up.
questions.probe: Who pays for cluster capacity today?

questions.q: When a node or a workload fails at night, who knows first?
questions.why: Observability without an owner is a dashboard nobody reads.
questions.need: A failure at night is seen by someone who acts
questions.how: Route cluster alerts to a named owner
questions.listen: If developers find out first, monitoring does not cover the platform.
questions.probe: What was the last cluster incident, and how long did it last?

questions.q: Which clusters need to run directly on physical servers, for GPUs, latency or the edge?
questions.why: Some workloads cannot afford a virtualisation layer; the same operations should still apply to them.
questions.need: Clusters on physical servers are managed with the same lifecycle, policies and storage as the virtualised ones
questions.how: List the workloads that need physical servers and include them in the platform's scope
questions.listen: GPUs, low latency or the edge can justify physical nodes; otherwise virtual nodes are easier to run.
questions.probe: Which workloads need direct access to the hardware?

questions.q: Which applications run in containers today, and which are planned to move in the next year?
questions.why: Current and planned workloads size the platform and show its priority.
questions.need: Current and planned container workloads are listed
questions.how: List applications in containers and those planned, with dates
questions.listen: A list of planned moves with dates gives the platform a deadline.
questions.probe: Which application would be the first on a new platform?

questions.q: How do users and other clusters reach the applications: load balancers, ingress, service mesh?
questions.why: Networking is where clusters differ most and break most.
questions.need: Ingress, load balancing and traffic between clusters are documented
questions.how: Draw how traffic reaches one application from the user
questions.listen: Every cluster wired differently means every move needs network work.
questions.probe: Who manages load balancer addresses and certificates?

questions.q: Where do teams keep images and secrets, and who can read them?
questions.why: Registries and secret handling are frequent audit findings.
questions.need: Registries and secret stores are agreed and controlled
questions.how: List registries and secret stores with their access rules
questions.listen: Secrets in plain manifests or open registries are an early fix.
questions.probe: Are images scanned before they reach production?

questions.q: Who runs the platform as a product: a platform team, each team for itself, or an outside provider?
questions.why: Ownership decides whether self-service within limits can exist.
questions.need: A platform owner and its service are named
questions.how: Name who owns clusters, upgrades and the catalogue
questions.listen: Without a platform owner, every team rebuilds the same things.
questions.probe: What would the platform team stop doing if clusters looked after themselves?

questions.q: Do some applications need virtual machines and containers side by side for a while?
questions.why: Mixed estates need one platform for both, or clear boundaries.
questions.need: Workloads that need machines and containers together are known
questions.how: List applications that span virtual machines and containers
questions.listen: Applications half moved need one network and one policy across both.
questions.probe: Which database stays on a virtual machine while its application moves to containers?
